requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The fix is in TypeCollector, the code the analyzer and the source generator share. When two members share a key, it now keeps the first member and skips the second instead of calling Dictionary.Add again (which throws). When a member uses a different key kind from the others, it reports the existing diagnostic and skips the member. Before, it went on to dereference a null key. These guards are applied in both member-collection loops. New analyzer tests check that types marked `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` still get MsgPack004, MsgPack015, MsgPack003 and MsgPack005. Another test checks they do not get MsgPack011, MsgPack016 or MsgPack017. Execution tests check that no formatter is generated for such a type and that it round-trips through the dynamic resolver. A new README section describes this behavior.
story.why: The issue reports that the analyzer stopped working for suppressed types in 3.1.1. The change assumes the cause is an analyzer crash (an exception from TypeCollector) on duplicate or mixed keys, which stops it reporting anything. The test names ('WithoutAnalyzerFailure') point to the same idea. Nothing in the diff checks SuppressSourceGeneration directly, and no part of the diff ties the crash to 3.1.1 or to suppressed types specifically.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new user-facing section listing which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types, including MsgPack012, which no test covers.

TypeCollector.cs line 1007 changes the diagnostic location lookup from `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?` to `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. This is unrelated to the bug and is not mirrored at line 1147.
The same guards also change source-generator behavior for normal (non-suppressed) types, because TypeCollector is shared.
story.confidence_overview: Medium that the guards remove a real crash path (Dictionary.Add on a duplicate key; `intKey!.Value` on a null key). Low to medium that this is the actual root cause of REQ-2234: no suppression-specific code changed, and nothing shows the new tests fail without the fix. High that there is no public API, wire-format or new-rule change.

findings.description: Claim C6 disputed: C6 claims 'Nothing in the diff shows they fail without the TypeCollector change' while citing SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 80-144. TypeCollector.cs directly shows those three tests fail with analyzer exceptions (AD0001) without the change: without lines 1023-1026 and 1039-1042, DuplicateIntKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure and DuplicateStringKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure call intMembers.Add / stringMembers.Add with duplicate keys and throw ArgumentException; without continue on line 1008, MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure enters if (isIntKey) on line 1012 with intKey == null and throws InvalidOperationException at intKey!.Value on line 1019.

The lookup changed from `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation()` to `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. Members with no source syntax (for example inherited from a base type in a referenced assembly) have an empty array, so this now throws IndexOutOfRangeException. That reintroduces an analyzer crash of the kind this change is meant to fix. The second loop at line 1147 keeps FirstOrDefault, so the two loops now differ.

No code in the diff is keyed on SuppressSourceGeneration, and the fix applies to all types. The diff does not show why the analyzer failed only for suppressed types since 3.1.1. If the real regression is elsewhere (for example suppressed types being skipped or handled differently), it may remain unfixed.

`continue` skips everything after it for a member with the wrong key kind. That includes the formatter-attribute lookup at line 1045 and any later per-member validation, so those diagnostics are no longer reported for that member.
The README says MsgPack012 (type accessibility) is reported for suppressed types, but no test checks it.

Replacing item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() with item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax().GetLocation() throws IndexOutOfRangeException when a [MessagePackObject] inherits a [Key] property with a mismatched key kind from a base class in a referenced metadata assembly (where DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty). TypeCollector collects inherited members (see GetDeclaringTypeIfColliding on line 1021), and the parallel field loop on line 1147 still uses FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation().
